findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no row for the topic. That happens, for example, when they were notified by a mention or a watched category but never visited the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 from the unsubscribe link in their email. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle the nil case.

findings.title: Notification level saved directly, so auto-tracking can undo the unsubscribe
findings.body: `tu.save!` writes `notification_level` without setting `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and without publishing the MessageBus change. `TopicUser.change` normally does all three. `auto_track` and the SQL in `update_last_read` both re-track a topic when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`. So a user who never changed this topic manually can be silently moved back to tracking after reading or posting, which reverses the unsubscribe. Open clients also never learn about the new level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

findings.title: State-changing GET endpoint that lowers the level again on every visit
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is a GET route and changes notification state on each request, with no confirmation and no CSRF protection. Link prefetchers, email security scanners, browser reloads or a cross-site `` tag can trigger it. Because each call drops the level one step (watching/tracking -> regular, regular -> muted), a second hit silently mutes a topic the user only meant to stop watching. Make the change idempotent, for example by recording the target level, or require a POST/confirmation step.

findings.title: Client-side navigation to the unsubscribe page does not unsubscribe
findings.body: The Ember route loads the topic with `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls `/t/:id.json` (topics#show), not the `unsubscribe` endpoint. Only a full server page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` changes the notification level. If the user reaches this route through an in-app transition, the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications" but nothing changes on the server.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} from every caller
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` use it for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link; the spec had to be patched to pass the argument for exactly this reason. Use a separate key for the per-topic sentence, or include it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: Message says notifications stop even when the user was only moved to regular
findings.body: The page always shows "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". A user who was watching or tracking is only moved to `regular`, which still notifies them on mentions and replies. The text overstates what the action did.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested cases include the slug redirect, logged-out access, a missing TopicUser row, and the level transitions (watching -> regular, regular -> muted).
